summary: Sales are growing and the company is profitable, but the stock already prices in several more years of fast growth, and one large lawsuit is unresolved [1][2]. The evidence supports holding what you own and waiting for the ruling rather than adding now [3].
bull: Revenue grew faster than the year before for the third quarter in a row [1].
The company makes more cash than its reported profit, which is a healthy sign [1].
bear: At about 40 times next year's earnings the price leaves little room for a miss [2].
A lawsuit that could cost up to a tenth of a year's sales has no ruling date yet [3].

angles.name: Business & market
angles.summary: Growth and cash flow are strong, but the valuation already assumes it continues [1][2].

angles.name: Regulation & legal
angles.summary: One open lawsuit is the main unknown. The company disclosed it in its annual report [3].

angles.name: Industry & competition
angles.summary: Demand in the industry is growing and two rivals report weaker growth [4].

angles.name: People & operations
angles.summary: No leadership changes in the last year. Insiders sold only under pre-arranged plans [5].

angles.name: Skeptic
angles.summary: The strongest case against is the price, not the business [2].

agreements: The business itself is healthy and growing.
disagreements: Business & market and the Skeptic differ on whether the current price is too high.
whatWouldChangeMyMind: A ruling in the lawsuit, or growth falling below the pace the price assumes.
